why: Correct the workshop roof and front framing while preserving its painted style and two-cell footprint.
day_prompt:
Create a corrected replacement sprite for the small Brazilian community workshop shown in reference image 1. Reference images 1 and 2 establish the EXACT painted game style and human scale ONLY. Do not copy the roof geometry of image 1. Reconstruct the whole building from a coherent orthographic architectural model.
The workshop has an open FRONT gable face on the RIGHT, and a creamy LEFT side wall with teal shutters. Four vertical timber corner posts support a SMALL low-pitched terracotta tiled gable roof with modest equal eaves. No oversized roof. Adults could stand comfortably under the open-front lintel. Roof occupies about the upper third of the building, walls/opening the lower two-thirds. The room is a compact square two-cell footprint. The roof ridge is centered over the room.
CRITICAL PROJECTION: exactly 2:1 orthographic ground plane. All receding rightward-downward horizontals have +0.5 slope, all rightward-upward horizontals have -0.5 slope. Roof ridge and LEFT side eave are parallel +0.5. Front lintel, front fascia and front floor edge are parallel -0.5. Shelf and workbench long edges run in that same front direction. Vertical posts are vertical. No perspective vanishing points. Do not let the roof ridge be steeper than the side eave.
Same workshop details: terracotta tile roof, warm timber frame, cream limewashed wall, teal shutters, low red-brick knee walls, a human-height wooden workbench with saw/mallet and tool rack inside, neatly stacked timber, small tropical plants and clay pot. Keep the palette and hand-painted texture of the references, broad readable forms. Small integral stone foundation ONLY, no gray platform or large ground tile. Full single sprite centered on a square truly transparent canvas with margins. Warm upper-left daylight, no backdrop, no people, no text, no external cast shadow, no solar panels.
night_prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. Image 1 is the accepted corrected workshop DAY sprite, and the edit target. Image 2 is the previous workshop NIGHT sprite, LIGHTING REFERENCE ONLY. Create the night-lighting counterpart of image 1.
Lock every pixel position and shape from image 1: same roof ridge, eaves, walls, post heights, front framing, tools, workbench, window, plants, base, crop, canvas dimensions and transparent silhouette. Do not redraw architecture, change perspective, resize, move objects, add a platform or change the alpha boundary. Only change illumination and surface colors.
Match image 2's cool moonlit terracotta roof, muted dark wood, cool cream walls and plants, with bright warm amber light from the teal side window and a soft warmly lit workbench/tool rack inside the open front. Roof, stone and foliage must not glow warm or emit light. No visible light source added, no background or external cast shadows. Transparent RGBA PNG, same square dimensions as image 1. Keep the corrected building exactly registered to the day version.
Use the same 1254 by 1254 pixel canvas as image 1.
review: Trace side foundation, side eave and roof ridge together; compare front foundation, lintel and workbench. Check both sprites on the actual grid and in the village.
